constant_registration.evidence: Vanhoof et al. 2021 (PMC7812139, doi 10.1111/joa.13314) Methods 2.3, Equations (1)-(2): 'For both gibbons and macaques, the average muscle density is 0.0011 g/mm3 (SD <0.0001 g/mm3), which is almost equal to the density defined for human muscles (0.00106 g/mm3) (Ward and Lieber, 2005). ... Therefore, the density value of 0.0011 g/mm3 is used in the calculation of the PCSA for all muscles in this study.' PCSA = mass/(FL x density); density measured per Eq. 2 (extrinsic muscles only); pennation omitted by the authors' stated omission (cos 0-30 deg = 1-0.87); multi-belly PCSA = sum of bellies.
constant_registration.key_connection: the funnel's inherited 1060 kg/m3 is the paper's CITED HUMAN constant (Ward & Lieber 2005); the paper measured and used its own 1.1 g/cm3 for these very specimens -- the funnel had registered the citation, not the source's arithmetic

residual_structure_the_source_truth.mechanism_named: the paper itself: 'For the small intrinsic hand muscles we were not able to accurately determine the muscle volume using the submersion method. This is a source data-quality structure (print register), not transcription noise: double-entry agreement was 1.0 (654/654)

successor_scope_named: the source cannot support a 2%-closure admission floor beyond 66.97% at its own stated constant -- that is the honest ceiling of this arithmetic and this print register. Two DERIVED (not fitted) doors exist for a successor, each requiring a NEW prereg: (a) a print-register error model from the paper's own declared precision (mass +-0.05 g, FL +-0.05 mm, PCSA +-0.05 mm2 propagate analytically into a per-row deviation envelope; a row passes iff its deviation is inside ITS envelope and the implied density is inside the paper's measured SD band) -- this re-derives the instrument instead of widening the tolerance; (b) consumers use the 438 law-verified cells + the per-muscle summary as-is, carrying the law-verdict conditions. Under no successor door may the constant be re-chosen against a pass rate.
